answer: Like nectar attracting both bees and mimics, an open agent economy needs proof that each identity is real. One mechanism is stake-weighted peer attestation: an agent locks a deposit as hard as quartz before it can transact, and established peers must vouch for it, each risking part of their own stake. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund many deposits and buy many vouches, so the cost of forging identities grows with every fake, while a public beacon of attestation history lets others check whether an identity's endorsers are independent or merely its own sockpuppets.
